summary: @or-sdk/permissions-cli preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated bundled payload
details: The package declares a preinstall hook (`node setup.mjs`) that downloads the Bun runtime from oven-sh GitHub releases into a temp directory, marks it executable, and uses it to run a bundled sibling file `math_init.js` (~727 KB, single-line, string-array-shuffle obfuscated with `_0x`-style identifiers and a >1000-entry lookup table). `setup.mjs` is itself obfuscated in the same style. The package's advertised purpose is a permissions-YAML upload CLI (`npx @or-sdk/permissions-cli upsert path/to/permissions.yaml`), which does not require a second JavaScript runtime or a large opaque init blob. Fetching an alien runtime at install time specifically to execute a bundled obfuscated payload bypasses Node-based inspection tooling and hands install-time code execution to code whose contents cannot be readily audited. This is the alternate-runtime dropper pattern (Example M, Scenario 2): the runtime install is fetched from an official source, but it is used to execute obfuscated bundled code rather than to run the package's normal shipped logic, and there is a clear purpose mismatch with the package's stated function.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
